# Desktop package skeleton and its pure modules (settings, links, shell PATH, bundled paths) ## What to build Create the new npm workspace `apps/graph-manager-desktop`, the Electron desktop app for graph-manager (KAN-86, spec `docs/prd/desktop-app.md`). It needs a TypeScript build, vitest and lint wired into the repo root, so the root `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` covers it on ubuntu, macOS and Windows. This task writes only the **pure, unit-tested modules** that later tasks use. None of them imports `electron`, so their tests run without an Electron binary: - `src/settings.ts`: reads and writes `/desktop.json` - `src/links.ts`: `classifyLink`, which decides where a URL opens - `src/shellEnv.ts`: macOS login-shell `PATH` - `src/paths.ts`: `bundledPaths()`, which finds graph-manager's server entry and graph-execution's CLI in dev and in the packaged app - a minimal `src/main.ts` that only shows a placeholder window, so `npm start -w graph-manager-desktop` opens Electron. Later tasks replace it. ## Context: files to read before implementing - `package.json` (root): `workspaces: ["packages/*", "apps/*"]` picks up the new folder automatically. Root scripts: - `typecheck`: `npm run build -w graph-execution && npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present` - `test`: `npm test --workspaces --if-present` - `lint`: `eslint .` - `apps/graph-manager/package.json`: an example workspace package (`private`, `type: module`, scripts `build`/`typecheck`/`test`). - `apps/graph-manager/tsconfig.json`: the compiler options to copy (ES2022, NodeNext, strict, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`). - `apps/graph-manager/vitest.config.ts`: the Windows tmpdir and autocrlf preamble. Copy the `include` style; the desktop tests need only `test.include: ["src/**/*.test.ts"]`. - `eslint.config.js` (root): flat config. `**/dist/` is ignored. Add `"apps/graph-manager-desktop/stage/"` and `"apps/graph-manager-desktop/release/"` to `ignores`. `apps/*/scripts/**/*.mjs` already gets `process` and `console` globals. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts` (lines 33–60): `resolveGraphExecutionPackage()` resolves a package's `package.json` with `import.meta.resolve`, falling back to `createRequire(...).resolve.paths`. Mirror this for resolving packages in dev. - `.gitignore` (root): `node_modules`, `dist`, `.graph-execution`, `__pycache__/`. Add `apps/graph-manager-desktop/stage/` and `apps/graph-manager-desktop/release/`. ## Patterns to follow **Package (`apps/graph-manager-desktop/package.json`):** ```json { "name": "graph-manager-desktop", "version": "0.1.0", "private": true, "description": "Desktop app for graph-manager (Electron): runs it on this computer or connects to a server", "type": "module", "main": "dist/main.js", "engines": { "node": ">=20" }, "scripts": { "build": "tsc -p tsconfig.json && node scripts/copy-pages.mjs", "typecheck": "tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit", "test": "vitest run", "start": "npm run build && electron ." }, "dependencies": { "graph-manager": "*", "graph-execution": "*" }, "devDependencies": { "electron": "" } } ``` - Pin `electron` to the exact latest stable version: run `npm view electron version` and use that number with no `^`. Install from the repo root: `npm install -D electron@ -w graph-manager-desktop`. This updates the root `package-lock.json`, which must be committed with the change. - `graph-manager` and `graph-execution` are workspace dependencies (`"*"`), so dev runs resolve them through the root `node_modules` symlinks. **tsconfig.json:** copy `apps/graph-manager/tsconfig.json` options. Set `"include": ["src/**/*.ts", "src/**/*.cts"]` and `"exclude": ["src/**/*.test.ts"]`, `outDir: "dist"`, `rootDir: "src"`, and `"types": ["node"]`. Electron's types come from `import ... from "electron"`. **Pure-module style:** inject the side effects (fs, exec, platform, env) as parameters with defaults, as graph-manager does (for example `terminalEnv(base, binDir)`). Tests pass fakes. **Test pattern:** ```typescript import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest"; // temp dirs: mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "gmd-")), removed in afterEach with rm(..., { recursive: true, force: true }) ``` ## Step-by-step tasks ### CREATE `apps/graph-manager-desktop/package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `vitest.config.ts` - As above. `npm install` from the root, then commit `package-lock.json`. - **GOTCHA**: `electron`'s postinstall downloads the Electron binary. That's fine locally and in CI. Unit tests must never start it. ### CREATE `apps/graph-manager-desktop/scripts/copy-pages.mjs` - Copies `src/pages/*.html` to `dist/pages/` with `node:fs` `cpSync`. It creates the folder, works when no pages exist yet, and is cross-platform (no shell `cp`). ### CREATE `apps/graph-manager-desktop/src/settings.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: ```typescript export interface Bounds { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number } export interface DesktopSettings { mode?: "local" | "remote"; remoteUrl?: string; localPassword?: string; bounds?: Bounds } /** The settings in `/desktop.json`; `{}` when the file is missing, unreadable or invalid. */ export function readSettings(dir: string): DesktopSettings /** Writes `/desktop.json` atomically (temp file + rename), mode 0o600 where supported. */ export function writeSettings(dir: string, s: DesktopSettings): void /** The saved local password, or a new one (randomBytes(32) hex) written to the settings. */ export function ensureLocalPassword(dir: string): string ``` - Validate with `zod` (already in the repo's dependency tree; add `"zod": "^4.6.7"` to the desktop `dependencies`, matching graph-manager). Fields with the wrong type are dropped. `mode` must be `"local"` or `"remote"`. `remoteUrl` must parse as an `http(s)` URL. `localPassword` must match `/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/`. - The temp file is `desktop.json..tmp`. On Windows, `renameSync` over an open file can fail with `EPERM`: retry up to 5 times, 50 ms apart. The repo does the same in graph-manager's `src/server/store.ts`; read it and mirror its retry. - `mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })` before writing. ### CREATE `apps/graph-manager-desktop/src/settings.test.ts` - Missing file → `{}`. Invalid JSON → `{}`. `{ "mode": "x" }` → `{}`. A round-trip of a valid object works. - `ensureLocalPassword` returns the same 64-hex value twice. - On POSIX only, the file mode is `0o600`. ### CREATE `apps/graph-manager-desktop/src/links.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: ```typescript export type LinkAction = "same-window" | "new-window" | "external" | "deny"; /** Where a URL the page opens or navigates to should go, given the app server's origin (`http://127.0.0.1:1234`). */ export function classifyLink(url: string, appOrigin: string, kind: "open" | "navigate"): LinkAction ``` - Unparseable URL → `deny`. - Same origin (`new URL(url).origin === appOrigin`) → `new-window` for `open`, `same-window` for `navigate`. - Another `http:`, `https:` or `mailto:` → `external`. - Anything else (`file:`, `javascript:`, `data:`, `chrome:`, `devtools:`) → `deny`. - `about:blank` with `navigate` → `same-window`. With `open` → `deny`. - **TEST** `links.test.ts`: - `classifyLink("http://127.0.0.1:5/runs/a/b/view/", "http://127.0.0.1:5", "open")` → `new-window` - `https://github.com/o/r/pull/1` → `external` - `file:///etc/passwd` → `deny` - `javascript:alert(1)` → `deny` - same origin with `navigate` → `same-window` - `http://127.0.0.1:6/` (another port) → `external` ### CREATE `apps/graph-manager-desktop/src/shellEnv.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: ```typescript export type Exec = (file: string, args: string[], timeoutMs: number) => Promise; // resolves stdout, rejects on error/timeout export const FALLBACK_DIRS = ["/opt/homebrew/bin", "/usr/local/bin", "~/.local/bin"]; /** The PATH to use: the login shell's on macOS, else `env.PATH`; on failure, `env.PATH` plus the fallback dirs. */ export async function resolvePath(opts: { platform: NodeJS.Platform; env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv; home: string; exec?: Exec; log?: (msg: string) => void }): Promise ``` - On non-`darwin`, return `env.PATH` unchanged. - On darwin, run `exec(env.SHELL || "/bin/zsh", ["-ilc", 'printf "\\n__GM_PATH__%s\\n" "$PATH"'], 5000)`. Find the line starting with `__GM_PATH__`; the rest of that line is the PATH. If it's non-empty, return it. - On rejection or no marker, take `env.PATH` split on `:`, append any `FALLBACK_DIRS` that are missing (`~` expanded to `home`), join with `:`, and call `log("shell PATH failed: ")`. - The default `exec` uses `child_process.execFile` with `timeout` and `encoding: "utf8"`. - **TEST** `shellEnv.test.ts`: - The marker line in noisy output (`"motd\n\n__GM_PATH__/a:/b\n"`) → `/a:/b`. - Rejection → `/usr/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/home/u/.local/bin` for env PATH `/usr/bin` and home `/home/u`, and `log` was called. - `linux` → env PATH unchanged, and `exec` was never called. ### CREATE `apps/graph-manager-desktop/src/paths.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: ```typescript export interface BundledPaths { serverEntry: string; graphExecutionCli: string } /** graph-manager's `dist/server/main.js` and graph-execution's `dist/cli.js`: under `resources/app.asar.unpacked/node_modules` when packaged, else resolved from the workspace packages. */ export function bundledPaths(opts: { packaged: boolean; resourcesPath?: string; resolvePackageJson?: (name: string) => string }): BundledPaths ``` - Packaged: - `path.join(resourcesPath, "app.asar.unpacked", "node_modules", "graph-manager", "dist", "server", "main.js")` - `path.join(resourcesPath, "app.asar.unpacked", "node_modules", "graph-execution", "dist", "cli.js")` - Dev: `resolvePackageJson("graph-manager")` and `resolvePackageJson("graph-execution")` give the `package.json` paths. Take `dirname` plus `dist/server/main.js` and `dist/cli.js`. The default `resolvePackageJson` mirrors `resolveGraphExecutionPackage()` in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts:38–58`: `import.meta.resolve(name + "/package.json")`, falling back to scanning `createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve.paths(name)`, with `realpathSync`. - It throws `Error("can't find ; run npm install at the repo root")` when a package can't be resolved. - **TEST** `paths.test.ts`: - The packaged layout with `resourcesPath = path.join("R")` gives the expected joined paths. Use `path.join` in the expectations, so Windows separators pass. - Dev with a fake resolver gives the expected paths. - Dev with the real resolver: `serverEntry` ends with `path.join("graph-manager", "dist", "server", "main.js")`. It only checks the string, not that the file exists. ### CREATE `apps/graph-manager-desktop/src/main.ts` (placeholder) - **IMPLEMENT**: `import { app, BrowserWindow } from "electron";`. On `app.whenReady()`, open a 1280×800 `BrowserWindow` that loads `data:text/html,

graph-manager desktop

`. `window-all-closed` → `app.quit()`. That's all; the next task replaces it. - **GOTCHA**: Electron loads an ESM main (`"type": "module"`, `dist/main.js`) fine on current versions. Don't use `__dirname`; use `fileURLToPath(new URL(".", import.meta.url))`. ### UPDATE root `eslint.config.js` and `.gitignore` - Add `stage/` and `release/` of the desktop app to both, as described above. ### CREATE `apps/graph-manager-desktop/README.md` (stub) - Two lines: what it is, and `npm start -w graph-manager-desktop`. A later task writes the full README. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` at the repo root pass, and run the desktop package's typecheck and tests. - [ ] `npm run build -w graph-manager-desktop` writes `apps/graph-manager-desktop/dist/main.js` and the `dist/pages/` folder. - [ ] No unit test imports `electron`. `grep -l "from \"electron\"" apps/graph-manager-desktop/src/*.test.ts` prints nothing. - [ ] The `settings`, `links`, `shellEnv` and `paths` behaviour matches the tests listed above, on ubuntu, macOS and Windows: the tests use `path.join` and `path.delimiter`, never hard-coded `/`. - [ ] `package-lock.json` has `electron` at an exact version under the new workspace. ## Validation commands ```bash npm install npm run build -w graph-execution && npm run build -w graph-manager && npm run build -w graph-manager-desktop npm run typecheck && npm run lint npm test -w graph-manager-desktop ```
